latentmixtures: latent class, profile, transition and growth mixture models via Julia

latentmixtures-package.Rd

latentmixtures fits finite mixture models for categorical and continuous indicators with the estimation done by the Julia package LatentMixtures.jl. It covers latent class analysis (lca()), latent profile analysis (lpa()), latent transition analysis (lta()), latent class growth analysis and growth mixture models, including parallel processes (growth()), multigroup models with full, partial or no measurement invariance, one-step covariates and three-step auxiliary models (r3step(), bch(), dcat()), class enumeration (lmr(), blrt(), fittable()), nested-model tests under MLR (compare_models(), scaling_factor()), publication tables (lm_table()) and ggplot2 figures (autoplot.latentmix(), lm_fitplot()). Estimates, standard errors and test statistics follow Mplus conventions and agree with Mplus on the validation cases shipped with the Julia package; the documentation of each function names the Mplus option it mirrors.

Architecture

  • R front end. The R functions take data frames and select columns with tidyselect (lca(df, q1:q6, K = 3, covariates = c(age, female))). They convert the data to numeric matrices (factor labels are kept for output), check that auxiliary data have one row per row of the fitted data, and format results (console output with UTF-8 rules, tables in text, markdown, LaTeX and HTML).

  • Julia back end. Estimation (EM with random starts, robust standard errors, LRT bootstraps, three-step corrections) runs in LatentMixtures.jl, called through JuliaConnectoR and a small bridge module shipped in inst/julia/bridge.jl. A fitted model keeps a proxy of the Julia object (m$jl) together with its fit statistics in R.

  • Persistent session. One Julia process serves the whole R session. It is started on first use, or explicitly with lm_start(), and loads the Julia packages once, so the start-up and compilation cost is paid once. lm_end() stops it; models from an ended session can still be printed but must be refitted for anything that needs Julia. lm_session_id() lets other packages (e.g. latentclasscausal) share the process and reload their own Julia code after a restart.

  • Threads. Random starts and bootstrap replications run in parallel on Julia threads. The number of threads is fixed when Julia starts: lm_start(threads = n), or the environment variable JULIA_NUM_THREADS, otherwise one per core.

  • GPU. lca() and lpa() (with diagonal covariance matrices) accept device = "cuda" to run EM on an NVIDIA GPU through CUDA.jl, which must be installed in the Julia environment. Standard errors and auxiliary models are then computed on the CPU.

Installation

Install Julia (>= 1.12), make it visible to JuliaConnectoR (on the PATH or through JULIA_BINDIR), then install the Julia package once with install_julia_packages(). See vignette("latentmixtures").

Options

None. Console output uses UTF-8 characters; its width follows getOption("width").

References

Lenz, S., Hackenberg, M., & Binder, H. (2022). The JuliaConnectoR: A functionally oriented interface for integrating Julia in R. Journal of Statistical Software, 101(6). doi:10.18637/jss.v101.i06

Muthén, L. K., & Muthén, B. O. (1998–2017). Mplus User's Guide (8th ed.). Muthén & Muthén.
